references.text: Balak had promised Balaam great honor and wealth to curse Israel, which explains his frustration over the blessings.
Balak expresses similar frustration after Balaam's first blessing, accusing him of blessing instead of cursing.
Balak's earlier attempts to get Balaam to curse Israel, and Balaam's response that he must do what the Lord says.
The context shows that Balaam had blessed Israel three times, which Balak refers to in his anger.
Joshua reminds the people how Balak summoned Balaam to curse Israel, but God turned the curse into a blessing.
Nehemiah refers to the event where Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, but God turned the curse into a blessing.
Clapping hands together is a sign of anger and contempt, as Balak shows toward Balaam.
Balaam is described as one who was summoned by Balak, confirming the story of the attempt to curse Israel.
Moses reminds Israel that the Lord your God turned the curse into a blessing because the Lord your God loved you.
